newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Basket buying sustains Belgian blue chip shares.
newsitem.headline: Basket buying sustains Belgian blue chip shares.

text.p: Belgian shares held steady on Monday, outperforming weaker neigbouring markets as buying in baskets of Bel-20 stocks continued from Friday.
By 0855 GMT the Bel-20 index .BFX stood 0.64 point or 0.03 percent higher at 2,172.35 with a moderate 688 million francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
Dealers said the basket buying appeared mostly to be linked to the latest new Bel-20 index derivatives products due to be launched by one large bank.
"Otherwise, shares should go down a bit with the weak dollar," one dealer added.
Higher bond yields and weakness in the neighbouring French market over election fears also hung overhead.
The Bel-20 had soared late the previous session after the traditionally volatile settlement of April Bel-20 index futures and options, to end one percent higher in hefty volume.
Dollar-sensitive retailer Delhaize held up well on Monday despite the weaker U.S. currency after shares in its U.S. unit Food Lion climbed on Friday.
Generale Bank rose 1.07 percent to 1,415 francs, benefitting from speculation about its future as a non-strategic asset of the planned French Suez-Lyonnaise des Eaux merger.
Insurer Fortis, which will be another non-strategic asset of the new merged group, slipped just 0.16 percent to 6,140 francs.
